teams.synopsis: Stole the writer's RB1 and earns the #1 spot for it — top-tier Hurts, but the Giants' offense is the fragile link.
teams.blurb: Tony Fkn Romo stole my RB1 and I won't forgive him for that, but I will instead rank him 1st to begin the season. The WRs are solid, and Hurts at QB is top tier. I like Warren, but if he booms like Bowers last year, we're in trouble. The main flaw is relying on the Giants' offense for your WR1 and RB2. Projected record: 11-3.

teams.synopsis: The Rashee suspension was drafted around — boom-or-bust WRs, but a deep playoff run is possible if it holds together.
teams.blurb: The Rashee suspension will hurt, but he was drafted with that in mind. The RBs are strong, and stacking Nix and Engram is smart. The WRs are boom or bust, but if BLR holds it together until Rice returns, the team could make a deep playoff run. Projected record: 11-3.

teams.synopsis: Might have the best RB duo in the league — Kittle at TE is elite, but weak QB play is the one flaw.
teams.blurb: This team might have the best RB duo in the league. The WRs have upside for big weeks with MHJ, Jeudy, Golden, and Deebo. Kittle at TE is elite. The only thing holding this team back is the weak QB play, with a lot riding on Stroud's shoulders. Projected record: 9-5.

teams.synopsis: The most consistently great team in the PFFL — strong everywhere except TE, where Loveland is the swing factor.
teams.blurb: The most consistently great team in the PFFL. Surely, The Minutemen have a ring, right? Jokes aside, this is a top team once again with strong players at every position except TE. If Loveland has a top-seven TE season, the league might be in trouble. Projected record: 9-5.

teams.synopsis: Easily the nastiest WR room in the league — already good enough to make the playoffs if Maye and Caleb break out.
teams.blurb: This is easily the nastiest WR room in the league. Hockenson at TE is solid, and Conner should be reliable at RB. The real questions are Maye, Caleb, and Kaleb Johnson. If they break out, this team could be back in the playoffs, though I think it's already good enough to make it. Projected record: 8-6.

teams.synopsis: The defending champ at 6th — a low floor, but Egbuka and Harvey hitting could put this team right back in the playoffs.
teams.blurb: The defending champ comes in at 6th to start the season, a fine spot to be in. Grits stole two of my picks right before me, so naturally, I like his team, and I think he did alright at RB after taking Puka and Brock in the first two rounds. The floor is low, but if Egbuka and Harvey hit, this team will be right back in the playoffs in 2025. Projected record: 8-6.

teams.synopsis: Lamar and the RBs are strong, but the WRs lack the upside to push this past yet another .500 finish.
teams.blurb: This team kicks off the tier of solid drafts with a few weak spots. Lamar and the RBs are strong, and the Andrews stack is nice. The WRs are solid but don't have the high upside I'd like them to. I expect RPM to finish yet again at or around .500. Projected record: 7-7.

teams.synopsis: The Burrow-Chase stack is great, but an older, injury-prone supporting cast makes this a real boom or bust.
teams.blurb: The Burrow-Chase stack is great and the RBs Walker and Cook are solid. But the rest of the starters are older with injury risk, especially Kupp, and the weak QB-heavy bench makes this team a real boom or bust. Projected record: 7-7.

teams.synopsis: Fighting the preseason odds again, but Gibbs, McConkey, and JSN give this team a real foundation.
teams.blurb: The preseason stories already have Ben fighting the odds, but LeGoon looks set for a better 2025. With a core of Gibbs, McConkey, and JSN, this team has a solid foundation. I'm also a fan of Dak and Njoku this year. Never want to see a franchise struggle for 4 years straight, so good luck, Ben! Projected record: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: Off a 2023 title and a near-bottom 2024 — the Taylor/Henry duo is strong, but the WRs don't inspire much confidence.
teams.blurb: Coming off a title in 2023 and a near-bottom finish in 2024, this squad is eyeing a bounce back. Taylor and Henry make a strong RB duo, but McLaurin, Wilson, and Olave don't inspire much confidence. Feels like a middle-of-the-pack team in 2025. Projected record: 6-8.

teams.synopsis: Starts low with Pitts and WR question marks — but if Jeanty delivers, this squad rises fast.
teams.blurb: This team has potential, but it starts low in the rankings with Pitts and questions around the WRs. The upside is real, though, and if Jeanty delivers, this squad might be worthy of a higher ranking next week. Projected record: 5-9.

teams.synopsis: CMC's age is a risk he's aware of, but Brown and Adams holding steady keeps this team in good shape.
teams.blurb: He admits his running backs are getting older and could get hurt, but I still trust CMC to be great. If Kraft takes a step forward, Cole is lined up for another strong season. With Brown and Adams holding steady, this team should be in good shape. Projected record: 4-10.

teams.synopsis: Usually ranks himself low and proves it wrong, but this year the weak RBs feel different.
teams.blurb: I usually rank myself low and prove it wrong, but this year feels different. My RBs are the weakest in the league, and the WR2/flex spots rely on unproven guys. It'll take some big breakouts just to stay competitive in 2025. Projected record: 4-10.

teams.synopsis: Punting QB and TE lands him last, but the WR room with Amon-Ra and Travis Hunter is legit.
teams.blurb: Punting QB and TE lands Rolls With Butter in last place to start the year. The WR room is legit with Amon-Ra, London, Tet, and Travis Hunter, and Hall/Hendo make for a decent RB duo. But with three rookies and plenty of question marks, 14th feels about right. Projected record: 3-11.
